title: WORLD.build seeds a CPU torch.Generator and draws directly into encoder/world_proj/qproj parameters already moved to `device` -- RuntimeError on every RUN_DEVICE=cuda run with WORLD_ENABLED=1
failure: RUN_DEVICE=cuda (a declared choice: train/levers.py `choices=("cpu","cuda")`) with WORLD_ENABLED=1. Line 112 builds `gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu")`. Lines 117-119 construct `w.encoder`/`w.world_proj`/`w.qproj` and immediately `.to(device)` them. The loop at lines 136-142 then calls `t.uniform_(-0.1, 0.1, generator=gen)` directly on those CUDA-resident parameters using the CPU generator. ATen's check_generator (torch/include/ATen/core/Generator.h:155) raises `RuntimeError: Expected a 'cuda' device type for generator but found 'cpu'`, so every GPU run with the world model on dies inside WORLD.build before any tensor is trained -- the exact defect class round1 found (and this tree already fixed) in FAB.build and SIG.build. Only the `w.keys` draw here is safe, because it fills a CPU-allocated `k = torch.empty(nmax, route_d)` first and copies it to device afterward (lines 145-147) -- the encoder/world_proj/qproj loop does not follow that pattern.
evidence: world/api.py:112 `gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu")`; :117-119 `w.encoder = nn.Sequential(...).to(device)` / `w.world_proj = nn.Linear(...).to(device)` / `w.qproj = nn.Linear(...).to(device)`; :136-142 `for t in list(w.encoder.parameters()) + list(w.world_proj.parameters()) + list(w.qproj.parameters()): if t.dim() >= 2: t.uniform_(-0.1, 0.1, generator=gen)`. Contrast the now-fixed sibling packages: fabric/api.py:189 `gen = torch.Generator(device=device)` (with the comment "THE GENERATOR IS CREATED ON THE TARGET DEVICE ... a device mismatch that only fails on the hardware you cannot test on is the worst shape this defect can take") and sig/api.py:121 `gen = torch.Generator(device=device)`. WORLD.build never received the equivalent fix.
fix: Build `gen = torch.Generator(device=device)` (matching fabric/api.py and sig/api.py) instead of `device="cpu"`, or move the encoder/world_proj/qproj construction to happen before `.to(device)`, draw with the CPU generator, then move to device afterward -- the same shape the `w.keys` draw two lines below already uses correctly.

title: The composition root's own wiring table documents live_vocab as Vocabulary.live_size(), directly contradicting LM.decode's frozen contract -- the exact critical dead-row-masking defect round1 filed would be reintroduced the moment this table is wired up
failure: LM.decode's frozen docstring (lm/api.py:484-488, 516-522) is explicit and detailed: the caller MUST pass `Vocabulary.size()` -- the full positional id count -- as `live_vocab`, specifically NOT `live_size()`, "precisely so that this boundary does not move when a row is retired ... a suffix rule would mask the wrong rows -- and on the probation arms most minted tokens were retired." This is the direct repair for round1's filed critical finding (decode masked live token rows 260-2XX because live_vocab was bound to live_size()). Yet compose.py's own wiring table -- the normative description of what argument each row supplies, read by K10/K11 and meant to be the thing a future implementer of the loop copies verbatim -- states TWICE, in two independent rows, that `live_vocab` comes from a live_size-flavored quantity: the assembly-time 'vocab' row (line 339: "live_vocab -- Vocabulary.live_size under LM.decode's spelling") and the per-flush 'judge_probation' refresh row (line 1098: "live_vocab -- Judgement.live_size under the same consumer's spelling"). Both are asserted as settled fact with no caveat, no TODO and no cross-reference to LM.decode's own docstring, which says the opposite. If the loop driver is written by copying this table -- which is its entire purpose -- every probation-heavy run (the docstring's own example: 217 and 224 of 256 minted tokens retired) reintroduces the exact -inf-on-live-rows failure a second time, at the wiring layer rather than the call-site layer where it was caught and fixed the first time.
evidence: src/lm/api.py:516-519: "`live_vocab` IS THE COUNT OF MINTED ROWS ... the caller passes Vocabulary.size() -- the full id count -- rather than live_size(), precisely so that this boundary does not move when a row is retired." versus src/spine/compose.py:338-339: "live_vocab -- Vocabulary.live_size under LM.decode's spelling;" and src/spine/compose.py:1097-1098 (the judge_probation row): "live_vocab -- Judgement.live_size under the same consumer's spelling." Both compose.py sites name a live_size-derived quantity for the argument LM.decode's own contract says must be the full size.
fix: Correct both compose.py rows to say `live_vocab -- Vocabulary.size() under LM.decode's spelling` (assembly row) and `live_vocab -- vocab.size() (NOT Judgement.live_size) under the same consumer's spelling` (judge_probation row), matching LM.decode's frozen requirement -- and when the loop driver is actually written, assert this at a call site or in a test, since two independently-worded rows agreeing on the wrong quantity is exactly the kind of error a single K-check reading the table cannot catch on its own.

title: The RESUME/replay path still measures bytes_per_token dropout-free even though the BUILD path was already fixed to measure it with dropout applied -- SIG's signature width and DATA's splice gate are wrong specifically on every resumed run with TOK_DROPOUT>0, which is goal B's own scenario
failure: The build (online/fixed) arm now correctly measures `bytes_per_token` with dropout applied (line ~309: `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`) -- this fixes round1's finding on that arm. But the replay/resume arm at line 253 still calls `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)`, unchanged. Reproduced end-to-end: built a parent vocabulary online (340 ids, 84 merges) over a repeating sample text, saved its id2bytes sidecar, then resumed with TOK_DROPOUT=0.3 via CKPT_RESUME pointing at that sidecar. `build_vocabulary` on the resume returns `bytes_per_token = 16.0` (the dropout-free measurement). Measuring the SAME sample with the SAME vocabulary through the training stream's own dropout (`_segment(child, sample, dropout=0.3, stream=child.dropout_rng)`) gives `bytes_per_token = 11.384` -- a 29% error in the number every resumed run's SIG window width (`derive.signature_width_bytes`) and DATA's splice_window gate are computed from. This is the exact defect round1 filed ("bytes_per_token is measured on a dropout-free segmentation ... SIG's one signature width and DATA's splice gate use a number the training stream never produces"), now live on precisely the branch that matters most for goal B: every run that resumes with regularization on.
evidence: tok/api.py:253 (inside `if read_path:` / `if replayed is not None:`): `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` followed by `vocab.bytes_per_token = _derive.bytes_per_token(len(sample), len(ids))`. Contrast the now-fixed build arm near the function's end: `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)` with the comment "MEASURED WITH DROPOUT APPLIED, because the contract says 'the COUNTING segmentation applies tok.dropout' ... A dropout-free measurement describes a segmentation the TRAINING stream never produces." Measured with the repo's own code: parent size 340/merges 84; child (resumed, TOK_DROPOUT=0.3) `build_vocabulary` returns bytes_per_token=16.0; the same vocabulary segmented with dropout=0.3 (what tokenize() actually produces during training) gives bytes_per_token=11.384.
fix: Apply the same fix already applied to the build arm: on the replay branch, measure with `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=vocab.dropout_rng)` instead of `dropout=0.0, stream=None` (the dropout stream is already minted before this line, at what is now line ~244). One measurement rule on both arms, matching the module header's own 'THERE IS NO SECOND ESTIMATOR' claim.

title: Checkpoint restore silently drops the per-entry `recon` score and never restores the store-level `gate_theta`, contradicting docs/04_CONTRACT.md's own claim that these were the fix for two of the four checkpoint omissions that 'each disarmed a live mechanism at the run boundary'
failure: docs/04_CONTRACT.md's MEM section states as settled fact: "Checkpointed additions: prob, recon, nsrc_max, gate_theta -- four omissions that each disarmed a live mechanism at the run boundary." Of those four, `prob` and `nsrc_max` are genuinely restored per-row/store (memory/api.py:219, :244); `recon` and `gate_theta` are not restored anywhere in the file. `_restore_by_block`'s per-row loop (lines 204-232) reads r["key"]/tok/src/pos/ctx/own/active/prob/use/last/born from the blob but never reads a `recon` (or `selfcon`) field, and neither `open_store` nor `_restore_by_block` ever assigns `store.gate_theta` from the blob -- it is left at `Store.__init__`'s literal default of 0.0 regardless of what a checkpoint recorded. Reproduced directly: constructed a store via `open_store`, then called `_restore_by_block` with a synthetic blob row carrying `selfcon=0.87, recon=0.42` and a top-level `gate_theta=0.35`. After restore: `store.selfcon[0] == 0.0` (not 0.87), `store.recon[0] == 0.0` (not 0.42), and `store.gate_theta == 0.0` (not 0.35). `gate_theta` is the adaptive write-admission floor and `recon` is the reconstruction/verification score EVAL's `verification_fit`/`wrongness_probe` are specified against; both silently reset at every resume boundary -- the boundary goal B's every forgetting number is measured across.
evidence: docs/04_CONTRACT.md, MEM section: "Checkpointed additions: prob, recon, nsrc_max, gate_theta -- four omissions that each disarmed a live mechanism at the run boundary." memory/api.py:204-232 (`_restore_by_block`'s per-row loop) restores tok/src/pos/ctx/own/active/prob/use/last/born only -- no `recon` or `selfcon` key is ever read from `r`. `grep -n gate_theta src/memory/api.py` finds it only in `Store.__init__`'s literal default (`self.gate_theta = 0.0`) and in `open_store`'s Gate arithmetic docstring text -- never assigned from `restored`/`blob`. Measured via the repo's own open_store/_restore_by_block: restoring a row with selfcon=0.87/recon=0.42 and a blob-level gate_theta=0.35 leaves store.selfcon[0]=0.0, store.recon[0]=0.0, store.gate_theta=0.0 after restore.
fix: In `_restore_by_block`'s per-row loop, add `store.recon[free] = float(r.get("recon", 0.0))` and `store.selfcon[free] = float(r.get("selfcon", 0.0))` alongside the other per-row restores; in `open_store` or `_restore_by_block`, restore `store.gate_theta = float(blob.get("gate_theta", 0.0))` from the top-level blob the way `tick`/`n_written`/`nsrc_max` already are (lines 240-244). (state_dict, the save-side counterpart, is still a stub, so this needs to land together with that entry point's own write-side of prob/recon/gate_theta for the round trip to hold.)

title: open_partition's LEVERS READ line names enabled, reservoir and prior_blend; the body reads none of them
failure: The docstring at line 120 declares "LEVERS READ: enabled, reservoir, prior_blend", but open_partition's body (lines 124-179) reads only the wire `dom.d_expert_slots` -- `dom.enabled`, `dom.reservoir` and `dom.prior_blend` are never referenced anywhere in the function. Confirmed by grepping the whole file: `dom.enabled`/`dom.reservoir`/`dom.prior_blend` do not appear at all in src/domains/api.py; those three levers are genuinely read only inside `observe` (which reads `enabled`, `reservoir`) and `prior`/`census` (which read `prior_blend`) -- both still-unimplemented stubs. So open_partition unconditionally builds a live Partition regardless of DOM_ENABLED, and its own declared LEVERS READ line makes a false claim about which levers this specific entry point consumes -- the same 'LEVERS READ list does not match what the body reads' shape round1 already found on fabric.build (norm_only/grow/halt) and tok.build_vocabulary (cand_window/mint_pmin/mint_novel), now present on a package round1 did not review.
evidence: domains/api.py:120 "LEVERS READ: enabled, reservoir, prior_blend"; body at :124-179 reads only `dom.d_expert_slots` (a WIRE, correctly separately declared). `grep -n "dom\.\(enabled\|reservoir\|prior_blend\)" src/domains/api.py` returns nothing. The three names ARE read elsewhere in the file: `enabled`/`reservoir` at line 218-219 (observe's own LEVERS READ, a stub) and `prior_blend` at lines 359/380/404 (state_dict/prior/census, also stubs).
fix: Correct open_partition's LEVERS READ line to what the body actually reads ("none directly -- see d_expert_slots under WIRES READ"), or, if DOM_ENABLED is meant to gate whether a live Partition is built at all (a null-partition arm analogous to WORLD's `enabled=False`), implement that branch here rather than only declaring the lever.

title: open_store's LEVERS READ line names 14 levers; the body reads 3 of them, and the other 10 (beyond the package-documented owners/wire exception) are never read anywhere in the file
failure: The docstring at line 137-138 declares "LEVERS READ: quota, owners, key_src, key_win, key_depth, evict, probation_frac, src_share, verify, recon_hid, recon_tok, topk, write_mode, write_gate" -- fourteen levers. The body (lines 142-186) reads only `mem.quota` (line 146), `mem.key_src` and `mem.key_depth` (lines 179-182). `owners` is separately and correctly reconciled by this package's own module docstring ("the 25th lever and this package's own code never reads it -- spine/assemble.py reads it to compute two of those three wires"), so it is not itself a defect. But `key_win`, `evict`, `probation_frac`, `src_share`, `verify`, `recon_hid`, `recon_tok`, `topk`, `write_mode` and `write_gate` have no such carve-out and are simply never referenced anywhere in src/memory/api.py -- they are consumed only by `write`/`read`/`blend`/`maintain`/`judge`, all of which are still-unimplemented stubs. An operator reading open_store's frozen contract to learn what this call consumes is told ten levers are read that are not, in the same shape round1 already flagged on fabric.build and tok.build_vocabulary.
evidence: memory/api.py:137-138 declares the 14-lever list; body at :142-186 reads `mem.quota`, `mem.key_src`, `mem.key_depth` and the three wires `mem.d_capacity`/`mem.d_owner_blocks`/`mem.d_source_slots`. `grep -n "mem\.\(evict\|probation_frac\|src_share\|verify\|recon_hid\|recon_tok\|topk\|write_mode\|write_gate\|key_win\)\b" src/memory/api.py` returns nothing.
fix: Trim open_store's LEVERS READ line to "quota, key_src, key_depth" (plus the owners exception already explained in the module docstring), and leave the other ten declared on the entry points that actually consume them (write, read, maintain, judge) once those bodies land.
